item.title: US Investors Are Finally Getting a Clear Shot at SK Hynix
item.description: Until now, it has been difficult, if not impossible, for American investors to bet on SK Hynix.

item.title: Memory Chipmaker SK Hynix Starts Marketing US Listing
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. kicked off its formal marketing process for its US listing on Monday, as the South Korean chipmaker looks to capitalize on surging investor demand for the high-flying memory-chip sector.

item.title: Standard Bank Warns of Flight From Sovereign Debt as Safety Ebbs
item.description: Investors seeking to insulate their portfolios against turbulence should increasingly look beyond government bonds, which appear to be losing their traditional safe-haven status, according to Standard Bank’s head of G10 strategy.

item.title: Ready for the Future, Ireland Is Also Vulnerable to It
item.description: Ireland may be a bellwether for how an economy can bet its future on technology and lose.

item.title: The Investors Scrambling to Keep SpaceX - and Elon Musk - Out of Their Portfolios
item.description: Christopher Bejnar has spent the last couple of months combing through the fine print of exchange-traded funds, emailing financial advisers and moving money into European stocks – all to keep SpaceX out of his $1 million portfolio.

item.title: Canadians Skeptical of Carney’s Push to Open Airports to Private Investment
item.description: A slim majority of Canadians oppose allowing private investment in airports, a new poll shows, as Prime Minister Mark Carney explores selling stakes in the publicly owned facilities to unlock funding for major infrastructure projects.

item.title: Citi Joins Small Group of Banks Running London’s Gold Vaults
item.description: Citigroup Inc. has joined the small group of banks that provide the vaulting and clearing services that underpin the gold market in London, the world’s biggest bullion-trading center.

item.title: Options Flash Bearish Yen Signal as Tokyo Stays on the Sidelines
item.description: The options market is sending a bearish signal on the yen, with interest-rate differentials remaining firmly in favor of the dollar and the Japanese authorities avoiding intervention for now.

item.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wilson Sees Rotation From Chips to Hyperscalers
item.description: US stocks will struggle to reach new highs as investors rotate out of some of this year’s biggest winning technology trades, according to Morgan Stanley strategists.

item.title: Stalled AI Rally Has More Eyeing Old-Guard Stocks
item.description: Growing doubts about sustainability of the AI rally are pushing more investors toward old-economy stocks, according to the latest Markets Pulse survey.

item.title: Are SpaceX and Tesla Hurtling Toward a Merger?
item.description: There’s growing speculation that Elon Musk will combine his two biggest companies.

item.title: Hungary Selling First Eurobond to Harvest Post-Orban Rally
item.description: Hungary is selling its first international bond since Viktor Orban’s ouster in April’s watershed election triggered a plunge in borrowing costs.

item.title: Intrum Returns to Europe’s Junk Bond Market After Equity Raise
item.description: Swedish debt collector Intrum AB is back in Europe’s high-yield bond market for the first time since a sharp jump in financing costs forced it into a restructuring.

item.title: Apple Supplier Luxshare Said to Plan Pricing HK Listing at Top
item.description: Apple Inc. supplier Luxshare Precision Industry Co. is poised to raise HK$24.3 billion ($3.1 billion) after telling prospective investors it wants to price shares for its Hong Kong listing at the maximum amount it had set, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Taiwan Authorities Search Evergreen Marine Premises
item.description: Taipei prosecutors and the Investigation Bureau searched Evergreen Marine Corp.’s premises on Monday morning as part of a probe into suspected insider trading, according to multiple media reports.

item.title: Fincantieri Speeds Subsea Buildout With Deals to Buy Four Firms
item.description: Fincantieri SpA agreed to buy majority stakes in four underwater technology companies, boosting the Italian shipbuilder’s presence in a growing part of Europe’s military buildout.

item.title: These Are the Sharps Actually Making Money on Prediction Markets
item.description: What it takes to win on Kalshi and Polymarket.

item.description: Here’s a couple things about prediction markets. A lot of it is pure gambling and speculation, much of it on things with very little economic relevance. Another fact is that in all likelihood, if you yourself started trading right now, you’d probably lose your shirt. But there is money being made by some dedicated traders, really focused on areas like politics and economics. item.title: Kioxia to Draw $18.5 Billion Inflows on Topix Review, SMBC Says
item.description: Kioxia Holdings Corp. shares may see passive inflows of ¥3 trillion ($18.5 billion), because of the potential jump in its weighting on the benchmark Topix index, according to SMBC Nikko Securities Inc.

item.title: Yen Undervalued by Up to 20%, Former Japanese Currency Czar Says
item.description: The yen should be as much as 20% stronger than it is — around 130 per dollar, a former top foreign exchange official in Japan said, pushing back against those speculating that the currency might continue its slide.

item.title: Philippine Economy Can Handle One More Rate Hike, Remolona Says
item.description: Philippine central bank Governor Eli Remolona said the economy can handle another quarter-point increase in the benchmark interest rate, suggesting policymakers are ready to hike again next month.

item.title: Nvidia Supplier Unimicron Seeks $1.4 Billion in GDS Offer
item.description: Unimicron Technology Corp. is seeking as much as $1.4 billion from a sale of global depositary shares, according to terms of the deal seen by Bloomberg News, capitalizing on an artificial-intelligence frenzy that has lifted the Taiwanese chip supplier’s stock more than 700% over the past 12 months.

item.title: CVC Capital Partners Raises €3 billion for Mid-Market Fund
item.description: CVC Capital Partners Plc has raised about €3 billion ($3.4 billion) for a new mid-market buyout fund, expanding its private equity franchise into smaller deals.

item.title: Novartis to Buy Cancer-Drug Firm Myricx for Up to $1.5 Billion
item.description: Novartis AG agreed to buy British biotech Myricx Bio for as much as $1.5 billion, adding an experimental cancer drug designed to deliver more potent treatments directly to tumors while limiting damage to healthy cells.

item.title: Ocado CEO Steiner to Step Down in 2028 After Board Tussle
item.description: Ocado Group Plc Chief Executive Office Tim Steiner will step down at the start of its 2028 financial year, following a boardroom tussle at the British online grocery delivery company mired in a stock slump.

item.title: ITV to Sell Broadcasting Unit to Sky for Up to £1.6 Billion
item.description: ITV Plc has agreed to sell its media and entertainment arm to Comcast Corp.-owned Sky Group Ltd. in a deal worth as much as £1.6 billion ($2.1 billion) including debt, a move that will reshape the UK television industry.

item.title: Johannesburg Sees Path to Ratings Upgrade From Moody’s Outlook
item.description: The City of Johannesburg, which is on the verge of financial collapse, said Moody’s Ratings’ positive outlook on the municipality’s credit assessment provides a path to an upgrade that the authorities will seek to achieve through better governance.

item.title: German Factory Orders Rebound as Iran-War Effects Fade
item.description: German factory orders rebounded, encouraging news as the effect of the conflict in the Middle East on Europe’s biggest economy begins to fade.

item.title: Singapore Files New Charges in Nvidia Chip Fraud Case
item.description: Singaporean prosecutors filed additional charges including money laundering against a key suspect in an AI server fraud case, part of the Southeast Asian nation’s growing efforts to clamp down on Nvidia Corp. chips being diverted illicitly to other locations including China.

item.title: Nvidia AI Server Delay Report Sends Asian Tech Stocks Sliding
item.description: Asian technology stocks slumped after a report that Nvidia Corp.’s next-generation AI server rack system has been delayed by more than a year due to manufacturing difficulties.
